chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abbad ibn Yaqoub, from Amr ibn Mus'ab, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The beginning of every Book revealed from the sky is "In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful". So when you recite "In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful", it does not matter if you do not seek Refuge (from the Satan); and when you recite "In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful", it will veil you regarding what is between the sky and the earth.'

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful (Basmala)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of reciting the Basmala according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) establishes the Basmala as the primordial opening of all divine revelations, highlighting its unique ontological status as a protective veil between the heavens and the earth. This narration underscores the sufficiency of the Basmala for spiritual protection, offering a distinct Shia perspective on the relationship between the Basmala and the Isti'dhah (seeking refuge) during Quranic recitation. It reflects the scholarly view that the Basmala itself carries the weight of divine invocation, rendering additional protective formulas optional rather than obligatory in this specific context.
